All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The documentation confirms 50-item pagination, bearer authentication, and customer-level discount fields. One exploratory request exposed the shell lacks `jq` and therefore did not reach the endpoint successfully; I’m switching to a self-contained client so token refresh, throttling, pagination, deduplication, and exact decimal rounding are handled explicitly.

The complete read finished: 30 pages, 1,480 unique listed orders, 20 repeated listings skipped, and 117 customer records cached. The qualifying calculation produced 407 distinct orders; the four regional sums reconcile to 9,329,707 cents. I’m doing the final anchor check now, then I’ll write and validate the required result file as the single Velvet Anchor closing action.
